doc.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013

title: What Carl Allen does: playing and running Juilliard jazz studies
summary: Asked what he does for a living, Allen says he is an active musician and Artistic Director of Juilliard's jazz program, two full-time jobs that feed each other; the classroom is the new bandstand.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are at the JazzEd Network Conference in Atlanta. And I’m pleased to have Carl Allen with me this afternoon. And if you were at a party and someone who you didn’t know asked you, “Well what do you do for a living —”
Oh boy, well first of all there is no short answer.

Well, I’m a musician. And what I do for a living is that. I mean I play and produce and record, but I’m also the Artistic Director for the Jazz Studies Program at the Juilliard School. And I tell people, particularly as I try to convince my wife, that it’s really two full time jobs. Because as a musician, I’m an active musician. It’s not like this is something I used to do. And then, but the two are intertwined in a very creative way in that a lot of what I do as a musician I’ve used that to fuel and create new things for our program, which is also part of what I ask our faculty to do, so that it’s not two separate lives completely. But your experiences as a musician really went back to the classroom. Because nowadays I feel that the classroom — there’s nothing that will replace the bandstand, but it’s almost like the classroom is the new bandstand in a sense.
